meta.scalability_note: 3 EU regions (Nuremberg, Falkenstein, Helsinki) + 1 US (Ashburn) + 1 Singapore; limited managed auto-scaling; max 48 vCPUs (CCX63); no global CDN edge network
meta.performance_note: 99.9% SLA for Cloud Servers; multiple datacenters per location for redundancy; no native CDN; strong bare-metal performance; low-latency EU backbone

AWS Amplify.note: No managed frontend/web app hosting platform. Apps must be self-hosted on VMs or containers.

AWS Lambda.note: No native Function-as-a-Service offering. Serverless requires self-managed solutions (e.g. OpenFaaS on Hetzner VMs).

Amazon ECS.note: No managed container service. Docker runs on Cloud Servers. Community tools (Portainer, Coolify) provide partial equivalence.

Amazon EKS.note: No managed Kubernetes. k3s or kubeadm on Cloud Servers is widely used. No managed control plane.

Amazon EC2.note: Broad VM portfolio: shared (CX), dedicated (CCX), ARM (CAX). Up to 48 vCPUs / 192 GB RAM. Competitive pricing.

AWS Batch.note: No managed batch compute service. Batch workloads require self-orchestrated solutions.

Amazon S3.note: S3-compatible object storage with standard S3 API. Available in Falkenstein and Helsinki. Pricing significantly lower than AWS S3.

Amazon S3 Glacier.note: No archival storage tier. Object Storage has a single standard tier with no lifecycle cold-storage option.

Amazon EBS.note: SSD block volumes attachable to Cloud Servers. Up to 10 TB. CIFS/NFS can be configured manually.

AWS Backup.note: Automated daily backups for Cloud Servers (20% surcharge). Manual snapshots available. No centralised cross-service backup management.

Amazon EFS.note: No managed NFS/shared file system. Self-managed NFS on a VM is possible but not a managed service.

Amazon RDS.note: No managed relational database service. Databases must be self-hosted on Cloud Servers.

AWS Application Load Balancer.note: Managed HTTP/HTTPS load balancer with TLS termination and health checks. Supports multiple algorithms.

AWS Network Load Balancer.note: Same Load Balancer product supports TCP mode (Layer 4). Less feature-rich than AWS NLB for UDP/TLS passthrough.

Amazon VPC.note: Private networks with subnets and routing between servers. Supports /8 to /24 ranges.

Amazon Route 53.note: Basic DNS management with A, AAAA, CNAME, MX records. No health checks, latency routing, or TTL failover.

Amazon CloudFront.note: No native CDN service. Third-party CDNs (Cloudflare, BunnyCDN) are commonly used with Hetzner.

AWS Direct Connect.note: Hetzner offers colocation in its datacenters enabling private connections. No managed Direct Connect-style service.

Amazon Rekognition.note: No managed computer vision or image recognition service.

Amazon SageMaker.note: No managed ML platform. GPU instances available for self-managed training.

Amazon Bedrock.note: No managed Generative AI / LLM service.

AWS Glue.note: No managed ETL or data pipeline service.

Amazon EMR.note: No managed big data analytics (Spark/Hadoop) cluster service.

AWS IAM.equivalent: Hetzner Cloud API Tokens / Project Members
AWS IAM.note: Role-based access management via project membership and API tokens. Less granular than AWS IAM policies.

Amazon Cognito.note: No managed user authentication or identity pool service.

AWS IAM Identity Center.note: No SSO or centralised identity management across accounts.

AWS KMS.note: Volumes support encryption at rest. No managed key management service; keys are customer-managed at OS level.

AWS Certificate Manager.note: No native managed certificate service. Hetzner Load Balancers support automatic Let's Encrypt TLS certificates.

AWS Security Hub.note: No managed compliance or security posture service.

AWS Config.note: No managed resource configuration compliance service.

AWS Shield.note: Basic network-level DDoS protection included in all plans. No advanced application-layer DDoS mitigation.

AWS WAF.note: No managed Web Application Firewall service.

AWS CloudTrail.note: Basic audit log of API actions available in the cloud console. Not as comprehensive as CloudTrail (no streaming, limited retention).

Amazon CloudWatch.note: Basic CPU, disk, and network metrics per server in the console. No log aggregation, custom metrics, dashboards, or alarms.

Amazon SNS.note: No managed notification or pub/sub service.

AWS Systems Manager.note: No managed infrastructure operations or patch management service.

AWS Cost Explorer.note: Billing overview and projected costs available in the Hetzner Cloud console.

AWS CodeBuild.note: No managed CI/CD build service. Hetzner VMs are commonly used as self-hosted GitHub Actions runners.

AWS CodePipeline.note: No managed CI/CD pipeline orchestration service.

Amazon ECR.note: No managed container registry. Self-hosted registries (Harbor, Gitea) are commonly used.

AWS CloudFormation.note: No native IaC service. Terraform provider for Hetzner Cloud exists (community maintained).

AWS IoT Core.note: No managed IoT connectivity or MQTT broker service.

AWS IoT Device Management.note: No managed IoT device management service.

Amazon SQS.note: No managed message queue service. Self-hosted RabbitMQ or Redis queues are common alternatives.

Amazon Kinesis.note: No managed real-time data streaming service.
